_about: The clubhouse ladder. A club can only lay out as many holes as its clubhouse allows ('holes'). Each step up costs 'cost' and asks for a membership and a reputation first: 'members' in all, 'tier_count' of them at the named 'tier' or better, and a course 'rating'. Paced against a well-run course adding a hole every three months (see tests): the first step comes in the first year, the pro shop in the second, the grand clubhouse in the third. The two top steps ask for Silver and Gold members, which only a club with a high rating ever gets.

levels.name: Starter clubhouse
levels.blurb: A hut with a kettle. Three holes is all a club this size can look after.

levels.name: Clubhouse
levels.blurb: A proper clubhouse with a bar and a locker room. Room for six holes.

levels.name: Clubhouse with a pro shop
levels.blurb: A pro shop and a members' lounge. Nine holes.

levels.name: Grand clubhouse
levels.blurb: A dining room, a terrace and a trophy cabinet. Twelve holes.

levels.name: Country club
levels.blurb: A ballroom and a committee that argues about the dress code. Fifteen holes.

levels.name: Championship clubhouse
levels.blurb: Fit to host anything. The full eighteen.
